newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian manufacturers seen cutting jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian manufacturers seen cutting jobs.

text.p: Larger manufacturers in Australia's most populous state, New South wales (NSW), continued cutting employment in the March quarter, despite expectations of improving conditions, a survey has found.

The survey, run by the Australian Business Chamber and the Colonial State Bank, found that while smaller firms with fewer than 100 employees were employing, companies with over 100 workers were cutting back.
In total, NSW manufacturers expected to shed 2,300 jobs over the coming year, which the survey said would translate to 6,900 manufacturing jobs nationally.

"This really brings home the core of our unemployment problem and indicates that under current expectations, unemployment is unlikely to improve at least in the short term," Chamber managing director Philip Holt said.
On the wages front, the survey found pressures remained muted by the standards of the past 10 years, with 68 percent of firms surveyed reporting no change in average wages and six percent a fall.

The March quarter survey also found the manufacturing sector experienced its traditional post-Christmas seasonal downturn, with production, sales, orders, profitability and selling prices all down on the December quarter.

"However, after adjusting for seasonal factors, firms did see their first increase in general business conditions in a year and the outlook for the June quarter is positive with 35 percent of firms expecting improved business conditions against 15 percent expecting further weakness," the survey found.
That optimism was based on lower interst rates, signs of an improving housing sector and, to a lesser extent, Olympics-related activity.

For Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen a rise in raw material costs in the March quarter was of some concern because if the rice cycle was in upswing, it could further squeeze manufacturers profits.
"From a macro perspective, weak selling prices are good for inflation but they do little to assist profits and future employment," he said.
